tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent with multiple explicit trigger phrases ('why is my GuardDuty bill so high', 'reduce GuardDuty costs', etc.), and while it does mention some implementation details at the end, the bulk of the description is user-intent focused and concise enough as a short paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize GuardDuty spend, or reports an unexpected GuardDuty cost increase or an expensive protection plan. Activate on requests like "why is my GuardDuty bill so high", "reduce GuardDuty costs"...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is focused on GuardDuty-specific billing mechanics, workflow steps, and non-obvious cost behaviors rather than general concepts the agent already knows. It jumps straight into domain-specific procedures and defers detailed reference data to linked files.
tests.evidence: Runtime Monitoring offsets VPC Flow Log charges — for instances the Runtime Monitoring agent covers, GuardDuty stops charging for VPC Flow Log processing.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (billing tables, API call details, opportunity check definitions) is explicitly deferred to references/ files rather than embedded in the body, even within conditional workflow steps.
tests.evidence: For the full per-plan metric/unit/pricing table, the two critical billing behaviors, and byte-to-GB/TB conversions, load [references/billing-model.md](references/billing-model.md)

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three reference files are linked with markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies a clear condition or purpose for loading, e.g., tied to a specific workflow step and use case.
tests.evidence: load [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md) when identifying which plan drives a charge or reasoning about the Runtime Monitoring offset.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root with no traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations like the read-only API boundary and validation step are prescriptive and exact, while analysis and reporting steps explain rationale (e.g., security-value framing) giving the agent reasoning-based freedom.
tests.evidence: Never recommend disabling a plan purely on cost. Assign each finding a severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO) and, where a usage/cost signal exists, an estimated monthly saving.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple signals exist (Cost Explorer vs usage metrics), a clear default and fallback order is given rather than an equal menu.
tests.evidence: prefer Cost Explorer as the dollar signal, reconciled against the usage metrics... If neither Cost Explorer nor usage metrics are available, still report configuration findings

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (scope, inventory, collect metrics, analyze, validate, report) that applies to any GuardDuty cost review rather than a single instance task.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope... Step 4: Analyze cost optimization opportunities. Rank each enabled protection plan by its share of total GuardDuty spend

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Known Quirks' section documenting concrete, non-obvious environment facts the agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence: Your own log configuration does not change GuardDuty cost — do not recommend turning off customer VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, or S3 data events to reduce GuardDuty spend

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a report and provides a dedicated report template asset referenced in the workflow.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline in the body; the severity table is short (6 rows) and the full report template is offloaded to assets/.
tests.evidence:
| Severity | Definition | SLA |
|----------|------------|-----|
| CRITICAL | Runaway cost causing large ongoing overspend | Fix within 24–48 hours |

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is linked in Step 6 of the workflow.
tests.evidence: [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the exact condition for loading it — when generating the report in Step 6.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The workflow is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N' naming, matching the required format.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to self-check its findings for correctness before producing the report, covering sum accuracy, unit conversions, and framing rules.
tests.evidence: Step 5: Validate findings. Before writing the report, self-check the findings: confirm estimated savings sum correctly and each traces to a cited metric or cost signal... Drop or re-label any finding that fails these checks.
